title: HTTP Methods
definition: Standardized action verbs used in HTTP requests to indicate the desired operation to be performed on the target resource.
simpleExplanation:
If the URL `/articles` is the noun, the HTTP Method is the verb. 
GET = Read.
POST = Create.
PUT = Completely Replace.
PATCH = Partially Update.
DELETE = Destroy.
realWorldExample: When you type `google.com` into your browser and press enter, your browser ALWAYS sends a `GET` request. When you fill out a 'Sign Up' form and click submit, your browser usually sends a `POST` request containing your password hidden inside the request body.

basic: Which HTTP method is used to create new data?
intermediate: What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?

answers.question: PUT vs PATCH?
answers.answer: PUT is a full replacement. If a user has {name, email, age} and you send a PUT with just {age: 30}, the name and email are wiped out. PATCH is a partial update. If you send a PATCH with {age: 30}, it ONLY updates the age and leaves the name and email intact.
